title: Shell Norco C2 splitter PV-1767: +25 % ethylene (real plant, 2015 revamp)
source: Summers, de Villiers and Green, Chemical Engineering Transactions 69 (2018) 703-708, DOI 10.3303/CET1869118 (Sulzer and Shell): operating data before the revamp (April 2015); the revamp itself is withheld
question: The feed will shift to about 69 wt % ethylene and the unit needs about 25 % more ethylene from this tower at polymer-grade purity. What limits the C2 splitter, and what is the change?
data_note: Real plant: Shell's Norco C2 splitter, with operating data and tray hydraulics from the published paper (April 2015, before the revamp). The paper normalises flows to a 1,000 kg/h feed; PlantAgent assumes absolute flow = normalised x 92, backed out from the paper's 87 % jet flood at 4,877 mm. What Shell actually did is withheld from the agent and shown only in the comparison. The blind answer's +25 % design fails the documented polymer-grade spec (ethane in the product, at most 0.1 wt %): it cut the bottoms rate and reflux, sending ethane overhead. The engineering loop's design holds the spec (ethane 1 ppm at Shell's Feb 2017 feed), but the server did not verify it at 1.25x because it also set the feed rate.
suggested_questions: What limits the tower at the new feed?
What change reaches +25 % ethylene at polymer grade?
Which tower section is closest to flooding?
What happens to the condenser and reboiler duties?
